title: Request Scout — Bricklist & Soft Patches (Customer Signals)
summary: Working notebook that stitches recent customer notes into a short bricklist of small-surface fixes and experiment probes. Goal is to identify low-effort, high-usable-value patches that service teams can implement without a full roadmap ticket.
goals: Capture recurring micro-asks from support and AMs (last 8 weeks)
Prioritize fixes that are under 2 sprint-days or config changes
Sketch quick experiments that validate ROI before engineering investment
raw_signals: Multiple customers report non-deterministic token cost spikes when KV cache miss rate increases on chat sessions > 3 turns
Several enterprise customers asked for a visible fallback indicator when model routing switches to lower-cost variants
Field notes: customers confused by streaming vs non-streaming SDK behavior — leads to duplicate requests in some integrations
Requests from partners to allow ephemeral API keys for short-lived test harnesses
Requests for a tiny UI in Console to inspect per-request batching stats (shows if request was batched or single)
prioritized_requests: Expose 'last-routing-reason' in request metadata (small API response header) — helps debugging and SLA investigations
Add a KV cache miss metric per-client that surfaces on Console (toggleable) — low backend effort, high observability value
Create a Console banner explaining streaming semantics and SDK mismatch patterns
Support ephemeral API key generation for 1-hour test harnesses
Introduce 'batching_advice' hint in logs: suggest enabling small-batch mode when throughput < X TPS
proposed_patches: API header: X-Redwood-Routing-Reason (string) — implement as a passthrough from router layer (effort: small)
Metric: redwood.kvcache.client_miss_rate — aggregate at 1m and surface in Console under 'advanced metrics' (effort: small-medium)
Console: streaming quick-help card — static markdown + link to SDK snippet (effort: small)
Auth service: ephemeral key endpoint with 1-hour TTL, scoped to test orgs only (effort: medium)
Logs: batching_advice heuristic — add rule in request-evaluator to emit guidance when avg tokens per request < threshold (effort: small)
quick-effort-estimates: X-Redwood-Routing-Reason header — ~1 dev-day (router + unit test + doc)
KV cache client_miss_rate metric — ~2-3 dev-days (instrumentation + Console tile)
Streaming help card — ~0.5-1 design/dev day (content + deploy)
Ephemeral API keys — ~5 dev-days (auth changes + policy + telemetry)
Batching_advice log rule — ~1-2 dev-days (heuristic + test harness)
impact-notes: Routing header: immediate decrease in triage time for CS + SRE, lowers MTTR for model-fallback incidents
KV cache metric: expected to reduce tickets about perceived 'token spikes' by surfacing miss patterns to customers and engineers
Streaming card: should reduce duplicate-invocation bugs from SDK misuse — measurable by a drop in 'duplicate request' support tags
Ephemeral keys: increases adoption for partners and PoCs; raises a small security review but scoped TTL mitigates risk
Batching advice: reduces token cost for low-throughput customers with few code changes on their side
open_questions: Should X-Redwood-Routing-Reason be returned for all customers or gated to orgs with debugging turned on?
What privacy implications for exposing kv-cache miss rates per-client? Need legal sign-off?
Do we provide UI to let customers generate ephemeral keys or restrict to SRE/CS roles?
What thresholds define 'small-batch mode' for the batching_advice heuristic?
Any backward-compat concerns for SDKs reading new response headers?
next_steps: Sync with SRE (Ethan) to validate instrumentation design and cardinality constraints — 2026-03-18
Open small RFC for routing header and batching_advice rule (owner: Maya) — target 2026-03-20
Create Console design ticket for streaming help card (owner: Priya) — target 2026-03-22
Scope ephemeral keys security review with security team (owner: Samir) — request meeting by 2026-03-24
Pilot deploy kv-cache miss metric to 3 beta orgs and collect feedback for 2 weeks
notes-to-self: Keep this doc lightweight. For any item marked 'small' — consider shipping as 'hackday' or 'sprint-plus' rather than full-feature rollout. Track downstream impact using support tag 'patch-scout' and metric 'cs.patch_impact'.
